question.question:
A US parent owns a euro-area subsidiary. Opening equity (a stock) is 1100 EUR million. Each quarter the subsidiary retains its full profit: 21.5 EUR million in Q1, changing by -3 EUR million each later quarter (negative means falling), for four quarters. At year end, before stress, a dividend of 0 EUR million is paid, leaving closing equity. Spot is quoted as euros per US dollar: 0.9 EUR per USD. The stress is applied once, at year end after the dividend: the euro depreciates by 40 percent, meaning the USD value of one euro falls by 40 percent (so the EUR-per-USD quote rises). Translate closing equity (not opening) into USD millions at the pre-stress and stressed rates; gross translation loss is pre-stress USD value minus stressed USD value. The parent holds a net investment hedge with notional equal to 25 percent of opening equity (not closing); its USD gain is that notional translated at the pre-stress rate minus the same notional at the stressed rate. Report the net translation loss in USD millions, defined as gross loss minus hedge gain, signed: positive is a net loss, negative a net gain. Use exact arithmetic with no intermediate rounding.

Answer format: use exact arithmetic through all intermediate steps, round only the final value half up to 4 decimal digits, and return only the numeric value interpreted in `usd_million` with no unit label or additional text.
